problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex minimization on a real, complete, second-countable Hilbert space E. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R and f(x0)−f(xstar)≤Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x,ξ) using a fresh IID seed. The jointly measurable oracle is unbiased, E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x), with E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ². Only gradient samples are supplied; budgets count individual calls, including batch samples.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is differentiable and ‖D(∇f)(x)‖≤L0+L1‖∇f(x)‖ everywhere, with L0>0 and L1≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform central second-moment bound σ², σ≥0; no exponential-tail or almost-sure noise bound is required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All parameters are public, including x0, L0, L1, R>0, Δ>0, σ≥0, ε>0 and δ∈(0,1). The objective and oracle distribution are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteVarianceGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid and spec.admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: A measurable output X must satisfy f(X)−f(xstar)≤ε outside a failure event; no particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: P(f(X)−f(xstar)>ε)≤δ, with probability over both algorithm randomness and IID oracle seeds, under a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Convex stochastic optimization with gradient-dependent curvature and only finite-variance noise, requiring high-probability objective accuracy, is a meaningful variant of the classical globally smooth benchmark.
